expects.query:
Using the `/vss-setup-behavior-analytics` skill, end-to-end and autonomously, deploy the `vss-behavior-analytics` service on this host and configure it to **raise an incident/alert whenever more than 5 people are simultaneously in a camera's field of view**.

**Environment & prerequisites:** A bare Brev host with Docker + `NGC_CLI_API_KEY` for image pull. `vss-behavior-analytics` is **CPU-only** (`gpu_count: 0` = skip GPU enforcement; `ANY` = no-constraint pool selector). A live message broker / perception input is NOT required — this task verifies the service is **deployed with the correct alert configuration**, so a container that restart-loops waiting for a broker is acceptable. Choose an app entrypoint and a config that make the FOV-count violation incident fire for the person class; do not rely on a default config that leaves it disabled.
checks: `docker ps -a --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -qx vss-behavior-analytics` returns exit 0 (the exact `vss-behavior-analytics` container was created)

`docker inspect vss-behavior-analytics --format '{{json .Config.Cmd}}' | grep -qE 'main_search_and_alerts_app.py|main_analytics_2d_app.py|main_analytics_3d_app.py|main_public_safety_app.py|main_composite_app.py'` returns exit 0 (an entrypoint that can produce FOV-count incidents is used)

`cmd_json=$(docker inspect vss-behavior-analytics --format '{{json .Config.Cmd}}'); app=$(printf '%s' "$cmd_json" | jq -r 'map(select(endswith("_app.py"))) | first | split("/") | last'); config_dest=$(printf '%s' "$cmd_json" | jq -r 'index("--config") as $i | if $i == null then empty else .[$i + 1] end'); config_src=$(docker inspect vss-behavior-analytics --format '{{json .Mounts}}' | jq -r --arg dest "$config_dest" '.[] | select(.Destination == $dest) | .Source' | head -1) && test -f "$config_src" && jq -e --arg app "$app" '([.app[] | select(.name == "sinkType") | .value] | last // "kafka") as $sink | (if $sink == "kafka" then .kafka.topics elif $sink == "redisStream" then .redisStream.streams elif $sink == "mqtt" then .mqtt.topics else [] end // []) as $destinations | (if $app == "main_search_and_alerts_app.py" then (([.app[] | select(.name == "numWorkersForIncidentGeneration") | (.value | tonumber)] | last // 0) > 0) else (([.app[] | select(.name == "numWorkersForFrameEnhancement") | (.value | tonumber)] | last // 0) > 0) end) and (([.app[] | select(.name == "fovCountViolationIncidentEnable") | .value] | last // "false") | ascii_downcase) == "true" and (([.app[] | select(.name == "fovCountViolationIncidentObjectThreshold") | (.value | tonumber)] | last) as $count | ($count == 5 or $count == 6)) and (([.app[] | select(.name == "fovCountViolationIncidentObjectType") | .value] | last // "") | ascii_downcase) == "person" and any($destinations[]?; .name == "incidents" and ((.value // "") | length > 0))' "$config_src"` returns exit 0. This follows the exact container's active app and config and proves the worker that app actually uses for incidents is enabled, FOV-count incidents target the person class with a count threshold of 5 or 6, and the active sink maps `incidents`.

The people-COUNT threshold is set on `fovCountViolationIncidentObjectThreshold` (an object count) — NOT on `fovCountViolationIncidentThreshold`, which is a persistence-duration-in-seconds knob. The two must not be swapped.
